extra.message: The `reportType` value is read directly from `req.body.reportType` with no allowlist and concatenated into a shell command string passed to `exec()`. An attacker (vendor or admin) can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. reportType = 'pdf; rm -rf /') to achieve remote code execution.

The `period` query parameter is used unvalidated in `path.join(LEDGER_DIR, `${vendor.id}-${period}.csv`)` and written with `fs.writeFileSync`. A value like `../../../../tmp/evil` escapes the ledger directory, allowing arbitrary file write.

`vendor.logoUrl` (user-controllable via PUT /:id) is used in `path.join(ASSET_DIR, vendor.logoUrl)` and read with `fs.readFileSync` without the path-confinement check that `renderVendorBannerAsset` applies. Setting logoUrl to `../../../../etc/passwd` reads arbitrary files, and this route is unauthenticated (no `authenticate` middleware on line 856).

`staffQuery` from `req.query.staff_name` is interpolated directly into the LDAP filter `(&(objectClass=person)(cn=*${staffQuery}*))`. The `escapeFilterValue` helper exists in utils/directoryClient.ts but is not imported/used here, allowing LDAP filter injection that can alter or bypass the directory query.

`updateReviewVisibility` (route at line 552 uses only `authenticate`, no `authorize`) performs no role check — it only validates the `sharingMode` string. Any authenticated user (e.g. a buyer) can set `sharingMode` to 'marketplace_staff' and hide/reject or approve any review in the marketplace.

`applyMerchandisingFeedPatch` parses `req.query.patch` as JSON and passes it unfiltered via `Object.assign({}, feedPatch)` into `prisma.product.update`. A vendor can set arbitrary fields — e.g. `status:'published'` to bypass the pending_review moderation flow, or `vendorId` to transfer ownership — since no field allowlist is enforced (contrast with the admin `applyCatalogFeedPatch` which uses MERCHANDISING_PATCH_FIELDS).
